strengths: Strong empirical results: 16.7% better MMLU accuracy at 50% compression over prior methods, with 1.28× inference speedup and practical memory savings enabling single-GPU deployment
Novel dual-mask approach well-motivated to address fundamental tension between preserving shared knowledge and expert specialization in MoE compression
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 models, 7+ benchmarks, with 16 random seeds, thorough ablations, and honest discussion of limitations
Practical efficiency: training-free compression in 2 minutes, task-agnostic design, robustness to calibration dataset choice without domain-specific tuning
Clever system co-design with bit-packing optimization that reuses underutilized Bfloat16 exponent bits to eliminate metadata storage overhead
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-documented implementation details in appendix
weaknesses: Pairwise merging design choice lacks rigorous justification—claims of superiority over combinatorial merging are supported only by limited evidence (Table 6), yet this is a fundamental architectural constraint that deserves deeper analysis

Weak theoretical grounding: Appendix B.2 analysis assumes independence which violates for Mixtral (0.26 correlation); no theoretical explanation for poor reasoning task performance (11.4% drop on AIME25 at 25% compression)
Random expert pairing justified only by showing search-based alternatives are marginally better, not by demonstrating random grouping is fundamentally sound or optimal
Fixed similarity threshold τ_sim=0.4 across all models appears arbitrary; sensitivity analysis (Figure 5) shows different optimal values for different models, suggesting model-specific tuning needed

Bit-packing scheme has limited generalizability: fixed exponent shift of 112 specific to Bfloat16 and current models; losslessness claims in Table 1 appear to be within measurement noise; Algorithm 1 bit manipulations lack clear explanation
Severe performance degradation on reasoning tasks (61.5% on AIME25 vs 72.9% baseline at 25% compression) limits applicability, with insufficient analysis of why reasoning suffers disproportionately
Moderate novelty: combines existing techniques (sparse merging, Wanda saliency, bit-packing optimization) in new way for MoE; individual components largely borrowed from prior work

Calibration sensitivity under-explored: robustness shown only on 2 datasets for 1 model; calibration set size (128 samples) chosen without justification; activation-aware scoring shows only marginal improvement over magnitude-only

strengths: Strong empirical results across four MoE models and nine benchmarks, achieving up to 16.7% improvement on MMLU at 50% sparsity with minimal accuracy degradation
Exceptional practical efficiency: 2-minute compression time (vs. 52 minutes for D2) and 1.8× end-to-end throughput speedup with custom decode-GEMM kernel
Solid theoretical motivation grounded in probabilistic analysis (Lemma 3.1) with empirical validation matching theory closely for Qwen and DeepSeek models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 16 random seeds, thorough ablation studies, and robustness demonstrations across calibration datasets and sparsity levels
Well-engineered system co-design leveraging BFloat16 exponent concentration, validated across models with zero perplexity cost from exponent shifting
Task-agnostic, training-free approach without requiring downstream task-specific calibration, unlike competing methods
Extends to higher sparsity levels (75%) and combines effectively with quantization, demonstrating versatility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core components (magnitude similarity, WANDA-based saliency, bit-packing) are incremental extensions of existing work with primary contribution in systems engineering rather than methodology

Gaussian independence assumption violated in Mixtral-8x7B (Pearson correlation 0.2612 vs. 0.0006 for other models), undermining theoretical justification for Lemma 3.1 without adequate discussion of impact
Bit-packing design is tightly coupled to 2-to-1 expert merging; arbitrary compression ratios require explicit mask storage, negating practical efficiency benefits and limiting scalability claims

Insufficient analysis of why fine-grained merging outperforms coarse-grained approaches: lacks quantitative breakdown of fine-grained vs. intermediate granularities or information-theoretic characterization
Missing insights into merging patterns: no visualization of learned masks, analysis of which experts merge together, or correlation between similarity/saliency scores and expert functionality
Comparison fairness issues: Wanda baseline uses 2:4 sparsity applied only to experts (different from NAEE's uniform application), and comparisons with recent quantization-based MoE methods missing
Hardware specificity: all experiments on RTX5090/4090; generalization to A100 or other architectures unclear; custom Triton kernel may not be portable
Limited statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests comparing methods; some differences fall within reported standard deviations
Hyperparameter selection under-justified: τ_sim=0.4 chosen from optimal range 0.3-0.5 but rationale for this specific value across all models not provided
